1. The rules

Strategy 2: MACD histogram bigger than the previous candle and Stoch RSI blue crosses above orange with blue below 50 → buy at that close. Sell at the close of the first later candle where blue meets orange.

Buy only if the filter is true:

  • A50 / A100 / A200: the last 5 daily closes above the 50 / 100 / 200-day average (intraday timeframes use yesterday's check)
  • B50 / B100 / B200: the last 5 candles of the traded timeframe above its 50 / 100 / 200-candle average
  • +ADX: also ADX(14) on the traded timeframe above 40 (TradingView "ADX and DI")
  • Baselines: NONE (no filter) and ADX (ADX > 40 only)

3. What it shows

  • 50 vs 100 vs 200 average: no clear winner. Every average-only version loses in total. The best one changes from timeframe to timeframe (e.g. 30-min: B200 +₹16k; daily: A50/B50 +₹6.7k; 1-hour: all lose), so the difference between lengths looks like noise.
  • ADX > 40 on its own is the best version: +₹39,897, positive on 15-min, 30-min, 1-hour and 4-hour, and beats random buys with the same filter in 88–92% of runs on those timeframes. But it's only 87 trades on one stock. ADX > 40 is rare (about 1 in 10 Strategy 2 signals), so a few lucky trades can decide it.
  • Average + ADX together leaves almost no trades (36–67 over all timeframes; 4 on 4-hour, 3 on daily), so those results mean very little. ADX > 40 already implies a strong trend, so the average filter mostly just removes trades.
  • ADX doesn't tell direction. ADX > 40 can also be a strong *down*trend. Adding "+DI above −DI" would keep only strong uptrends.

4. Next step

One stock gives too few ADX trades to trust. Run the same 14 versions on all Nifty 50 stocks (python experiments/strategy2_ma_adx.py n50) before drawing conclusions.
